meta.description: Bulk-query Ensembl BioMart for cross-database ID mapping, coordinates, and ortholog tables.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md
meta.evidence_limitation: R biomaRt 2.62.1 could not reach any tested Ensembl mirror or archive in this environment; the source is schema-correct and Python completed the corresponding live BioMart checks.

scientific_integrity.detail: Live outputs were constrained to Ensembl reference data and no biological claims were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill performs reference-database retrieval and makes no diagnostic or treatment claims.

methodological_ground.detail: The rerun verified correct ID-filter, attribute/filter, ortholog, and long-format GO semantics.

code_usability.detail: All current-source archived scenarios and two fresh batching scenarios ran; the only incomplete check is the external R mirror connection.

functional_suitability.note: All stated Ensembl gene-mart workflows are runnable; unsupported Ensembl Genomes advice was removed.

reliability.note: The helper validates empty input, classifies outage HTML, and adaptively handles HTTP 414 batches.

performance_context.note: The reusable helper is separated from concise examples and is bounded for large ID lists.

agent_usability.note: Failure modes and typed errors give clear recovery paths; R live availability remains an external caveat.

human_usability.note: Trigger language and examples are clear and aligned with common BioMart tasks.

security.note: Public read-only service use, XML escaping, and local validation create no credential or destructive-operation risk.

maintainability.note: The helper is centralized in scripts; examples deliberately import the adjacent module instead of maintaining copies.

agent_specific.note: The decision matrix, stable error surface, read-only idempotency, and related-skill escape hatches are strong.
